A1.justification: Both complete, readable 18-page PDFs describe SpaceDrive. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections A–C can be matched reliably, with no material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original nuScenes planning results, Bench2Drive simulations, counterfactual reasoning evaluations, and ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains the original planning, simulation, reasoning, and ablation results. Their retention from v2 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same shared 3D positional encoding, visual-token augmentation, coordinate-token replacement, ego-history encoding, learnable normalization, coordinate decoder, and training objective. No algorithmic or architectural revision is documented.

E1.justification: Both retain nuScenes open-loop planning, Bench2Drive closed-loop scenarios, and OmniDrive-derived VQA coverage. The appendix's perturbation conditions and qualitative driving scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 adds AlignDrive to the traditional-modular comparator group in both Table 2 and supplementary Table J. All previously reported comparators remain; the VLM-based comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged. Both retain six-waypoint prediction over three seconds and the Bench2Drive protocol of 220 routes covering 44 scenarios. No revised protocol accompanies the added comparator.

E4.justification: The positional-encoding, decoder, normalization, backbone, depth-estimator, pooling, LoRA, frequency, and loss ablations are retained unchanged. Appendix depth-noise robustness tests, trajectory-distribution analysis, failure analysis, and qualitative cases are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 specifies seed 888 in both versions. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests; no statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 2 and J newly report AlignDrive with Driving Score 89.07 and Success Rate 73.18%. Existing numerical results and qualitative findings remain unchanged, including SpaceDrive+'s 78.02 and 55.11% and its second-place ranking among the listed VLM-based methods.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and their mathematical definitions are unchanged, including positional encoding, token injection, coordinate decoding, and the loss formulation. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified spatial representation, improved coordinate reasoning, leading VLM-based open-loop performance, and second-best VLM-based Bench2Drive performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of spatial-token benefits, textual-coordinate failures, and depth robustness are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning absent explicit uncertainty handling and multi-frame temporal memory; the conclusion's shifted page break does not remove these qualifications.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A preserve the same implementation disclosures, including coordinate parsing, decoder construction, LoRA settings, hardware, training schedules, and controller setup. Project and code access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 84 to 90 works, retaining all earlier references. Additions include AlignDrive, Fusion-Poly, StereoAdapter, BALF, hyperspectral image super-resolution, and global solvers for 3D vision. Most enter existing citation lists without substantive new discussion or revised novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Editorial changes are limited to the arXiv version/date stamp and citation-related text. Existing explanatory prose, terminology, section ordering, and appendix organization are retained; there is no substantial rewriting.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and J each gain an AlignDrive row, causing limited text reflow. The expanded bibliography also changes page layout. Figures 1–3 and A–C retain identical visual content, and other tables preserve their structure.

improvement.justification: Adding AlignDrive to Tables 2 and J modestly improves benchmarking completeness by exposing a stronger traditional comparator: 89.07 Driving Score and 73.18% Success Rate, versus the previously listed leader HiP-AD's 86.77 and 69.09%. This improves context for assessing SpaceDrive without implying improved SpaceDrive performance. The benefit is limited because the method, original evidence, and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, while most added citations receive no additional discussion.
